extracted.intended_audience: public relations professionals, ICCO/CIPRA members, and journalists covering PR/association news
extracted.subtask_description: Creating short news-style press releases announcing partnerships or cooperative agreements between organizations, including a clear lead, attributed quotes, background/boilerplate, and links. Emphasis on factual meeting details, invitations/calls-to-action, and organisation descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline / title
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise, descriptive headline that names the parties and summarizes the main action (example: "CIPRA and ICCO strengthen relations and cooperation").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a clear, factual headline that immediately communicates the news (who + what). Keep it short and focused on the primary development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication date and category
rubrics_metrics.description: Visible publication metadata (example: "25th July 2016 / in ICCO News").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the date and an appropriate category or section so readers and journalists can contextualize timeliness and relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead paragraph summarising the news
rubrics_metrics.description: A short opening paragraph that states the core announcement (example opening: "The China International Public Relations Association (CIPRA) and the International Communications Consultancy Organisation (ICCO) have decided to strengthen ties and to exchange information, visits and experience.").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Front-load the who/what/where/when/why in the first paragraph so readers immediately understand the development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution of quotes with speaker and title
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct quotations with clear attribution to named individuals and their positions (examples: quotes from ICCO President Maxim Behar and CIPRA Secretary General Zhao Dali).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include at least one attributed quote from a senior representative to add authority and perspective; always provide the speaker’s name and title for credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of illustrative direct quotes to express intent
rubrics_metrics.description: Quotes that articulate goals or invitations (example: Behar: “We officially invite our Chinese friends from CIPRA to send a big delegation to Global ICCO PR Summit in Oxford this September…”).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quotes should convey motivation, intentions, or reactions (invitations, appreciation, plans). They make the news more human and provide soundbites for media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific action items / calls to action
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements of concrete next steps or requests (example: invitation to send a delegation; hope for CIPRA to join ICCO as a full member).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make any planned actions or invitations explicit so stakeholders and media know what will happen next or how they can participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meeting and participant details
rubrics_metrics.description: Named details of meetings, participants and venues (example: Behar met senior representatives of CIPRA and the Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs; meetings with Ambassador Li Daoyu, Secretary General Zhao Dali and Honorary President He Luli).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List key people present and their roles, and specify locations/dates where relevant to substantiate the announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on objectives and benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements explaining the purpose and expected benefits of the cooperation (example: "the achievements of the Chinese public relations business be promoted on an international level, and that the exchange of experience will be the productive motivation for success").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why the development matters: what objectives it serves and how stakeholders will benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background / boilerplate sections about organisations
rubrics_metrics.description: Concise 'About' paragraphs giving organisational background and scope (examples: 'About ICCO' and 'About CIPRA' sections describing mission, membership and founding).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include short boilerplates with key facts (mission, scale, founding date, membership) and website links so journalists and readers can quickly understand each organisation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of website links and references
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit links to organisation websites (examples: 'iccopr.com' and 'cipra.org.cn').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clickable URLs to organisational pages or further resources to facilitate follow-up and verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia: images and logos
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusion of relevant images and organisation logos (image URLs and logo shown on page).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add a photo or logo to increase engagement; include captions or alt text and provide image credits/permissions where necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social sharing functionality
rubrics_metrics.description: Visible share buttons for social platforms (examples: Share on Facebook, X, WhatsApp, Pinterest, LinkedIn, Tumblr, Vk, Reddit, Mail).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide social sharing options to increase reach; ensure share text and metadata (title, excerpt, image) are set for social platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timestamp/technical metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: Machine-readable timestamps and metadata included on the page (example: '2016-07-25 09:11:31').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include precise timestamps in the page metadata for archival and syndication; useful for news consumers and aggregators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone and register: formal/professional
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of professional, formal language appropriate for association announcements (as demonstrated by the text and quoted statements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a formal, factual tone for organisational press releases; avoid jargon that obscures the announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic and event context
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear mention of locations and events tied to the announcement (examples: Beijing visit, Annual CIPRA Summit, Global ICCO PR Summit in Oxford).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide geographic and event context so readers understand where actions took place and where future events will occur.
